correctness.rationale: T=MC-CM=CJ acts as (Tf)(x)=x^-1 integral_0^x (x-t)f(t)dt and is Hilbert-Schmidt (norm squared 1/6). T is injective because J²f=xTf. For nonzero eigenvector T*T f=s² f put u=J²f; the adjoint integral yields h=T*T f satisfying h(1)=h'(1)=0 and h''(x)=u(x)/x², so u^(4)=s^-2 u/x², u(0)=u'(0)=u^(2)(1)=u^(3)(1)=0. The potentially singular endpoint is covered by |u(x)|<=x^(3/2)||f||/sqrt3, so u/x² is L1, f is sufficiently regular to fix u^(2)(0),u^(3)(0). The weighted Volterra equation gives the unique solutions U2,U3 with entire parameter series (quartic recursion), each with L² second derivative. The two right-boundary equations are exactly the 2x2 determinant F(z)=0; conversely the boundary conditions and second-derivative identity imply T*T f=z^-1 f, ruling out every nonpositive or nonreal complex root by selfadjoint positivity. F(0)=12; infinite roots follow from infinite-rank compact injective T. Independently derived the first coefficients F(z)=12-2z+z²/40-z³/15120 by exact rational series, matching F/12=1-z/6+z²/480-z³/181440; checked diagonal kernel trace 1/6 and trace square 17/720 separately. Inspected actual source verifier implementation and boundary derivation.

originality.rationale: The 2018 Ramlau–Koutschan–Hofmann transcendental spectral equations concern J^n without x^-1 weight (constant-coefficient fourth-order ODE at n=2). The highly relevant 2024 Deng–Fischer–Hofmann paper analyzes exactly CJ, proving sigma_n~n^-2 up to constants, but not the explicit entire two-solution characteristic determinant for all singular values; the complete primary paper was read. Earlier Chuong–Hung covers weighted commutator boundedness. No stronger spectral formula found in Resultary or primary searches; weighted fourth-order spectral equivalences remain an originality risk.

value.rationale: An exact and convergent determinant characterizing every nonzero singular value (and geometric multiplicity) of a natural compact inverse-problem operator is a structural spectral result, not merely another asymptotic estimate or numerical finite discretization. It directly addresses the spectral-equation difficulty acknowledged in the 2024 CJ paper. It does not purport to provide closed elementary roots or zero-order multiplicities.

limitations: Operator exactly real L²(0,1) and T=x^-1 J², not arbitrary weighted Volterra operators.
Characteristic equation is implicit; approximate singular roots are not certified error intervals and root-order multiplicity/simplicity is not proven.
Historical equivalent weighted fourth-order spectral determinant cannot be excluded exhaustively.
